newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate eases, demand picks up.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate eases, demand picks up.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate edged down 30 basis points to 10.4 percent on Wednesday as demand for kuna funds picked up on Zagreb's money market.
Dealers put total trade at 45.9 million kuna but 2.1 million did not find buyers since lenders and borrowers could not agree on terms. Supply was 47 million kuna.
Fresh loans accounted for 37.9 million kuna of which 27 million were bought by one large bank.
All were call money loans, granted at a steady 10.5 percent rate, save for a smaller placement struck at 11 percent.
Insurers rolled over previous funds at a steady rate of 9.0 percent. Smaller one-week placement was granted at 12 percent.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Thursday weaker at 5.9917 against the dollar and slightly changed at 3.5686 versus the German mark. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
